# Climate Change and Renewable Energy

Climate change represents one of the most significant challenges facing humanity in the 21st century. The scientific consensus, supported by organizations like the IPCC, is that human activities — primarily the burning of fossil fuels — are causing global temperatures to rise at an unprecedented rate.

## The Greenhouse Effect

Earth's atmosphere naturally traps some of the sun's energy through the greenhouse effect, which is essential for maintaining temperatures suitable for life. However, increased concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and other greenhouse gases have enhanced this effect, leading to global warming.

Since the pre-industrial era, global average temperatures have risen by approximately 1.1 degrees Celsius. The consequences include rising sea levels, more frequent and intense extreme weather events, ocean acidification, and disruption of ecosystems worldwide.

## Solar Energy

Solar photovoltaic technology has seen remarkable cost reductions over the past decade, with the levelized cost of solar electricity falling by over 85% since 2010. Modern solar panels convert sunlight to electricity with efficiencies exceeding 20%, and perovskite solar cells in development promise even higher efficiencies at lower costs.

## Wind Energy

Wind power has become one of the most cost-effective sources of new electricity generation in many regions. Offshore wind farms can generate power more consistently due to stronger and more reliable winds at sea. Turbine technology continues to advance, with individual turbines now capable of generating over 15 megawatts.

## Energy Storage

The intermittent nature of solar and wind energy makes storage technologies critical for grid reliability. Lithium-ion batteries dominate the market currently, but alternatives like solid-state batteries, flow batteries, compressed air energy storage, and green hydrogen are being developed for grid-scale applications.

## The Energy Transition

The global energy transition requires not only deploying renewable generation but also upgrading electrical grids, developing energy storage, improving energy efficiency, and addressing the social and economic impacts on communities dependent on fossil fuel industries.
